key_idea: A window can become a palindrome with one swap iff it has 0 mismatched mirror pairs, 2 mismatched pairs with equal letter multisets, or 1 mismatched pair (a,b) fixable by an a/b taken from the centre or from outside the window.
sketch: Expand around each of the 2n-1 centres while tracking mismatched mirror pairs, stopping at the third mismatch; O(n^2) total for n=5000. Zero mismatches is always fine (swap two mirror positions, so the 'exactly one swap' rule costs nothing). Two mismatches (a,b),(c,d) work iff {a,b}={c,d}. One mismatch (a,b) works iff the centre letter of an odd window is a or b, or some a or b exists outside the window, checked in O(1) with per-letter prefix counts; borrowing from another matched pair inside would break that pair. Feasibility is not monotone in the radius, so test every radius rather than binary searching. Stress-tested against a brute force over all swaps.
